2. The necessary facts for disposal of this civil petition for leave to appeal, in short, are that the present leave-petitioner, as plaintiff, instituted Title Suit No. 51 of 2003 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Court No. 1, Khulna against the present respondent No. 1 impleading him as defendant No. 1 and another for specific performance of contract. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that the defendant No. 1, being owner of the land described in schedule to the plaint, contracted to sell the same to the plaintiff at a consideration of Tk. 1,40,000/- and on receipt of earnest money of Tk. 80,000/- out of that contracted consideration money executed a bainapatra in fovour of the plaintiff on 05.05.1998 on condition that the defendant No. 1 would execute and register the sale deed on taking balance consideration money from the plaintiff. That subsequently also the defendant No. 1 took Tk. 50,000/- from the plaintiff on 02.11.2002 by giving a money receipt and also delivered possession of the land in favour of the plaintiff on 02.11.2002. But ultimately on 07.03.2003 the defendant No. 1 denied to execute and register the sale deed when the plaintiff requested him for the same and hence the suit. 

 3. The defendant No. 1 appeared in that suit and filed written statement denying the genuineness of the impugned bainapatra. His specific case, as stated in the written statement, is that he never contracted to sell the suit land to the plaintiff, never executed any bainapatra in favour of the plaintiff and never took any money from the plaintiff. That some disputes arose in between the plaintiff and the defendant No. 1 relating to accounts in between 'them as they had business transactions and the plaintiff forcibly took some signatures of the defendant No. 1 on blank stamp papers on 30.08.1997 for which the defendant lodged a G.D. in the local police station; that the plaintiff might have created the impugned bainapatra using those signatures of the defendant No. 1 on the blank stamp papers; that the alleged bainapatra is forged, fraudulent and without consideration and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 6. Mr. Quamrul Haque Siddique, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioner has made submissions before us to the effect that in this case the defendant has clearly admitted the signature appearing in the impugned bainapatra to be his own pleading a case to the effect that the plaintiff took this signature on the blank stamp papers forcibly and thereafter created the impugned bainapatra in that blank stamp papers containing the signature of the defendant- No. 1. The learned Advocate has contended that in spite of this clear defence case of the defendant No. 1 all the courts below allowed the prayer for examination of the signature of the defendant No. 1 appearing in the impugned bainapatra by a hand-writing expert unnecessarily and most whimsically and arbitrarily with-out applying judicial mind at all. The learned Advocate, however, has submitted that the signature of the defendant No. 1 in the money receipt, since not admitted by the defendant No. 1, can be examined by hand writing expert.

 10. It should be mentioned here that this suit was once decreed ex-parte and for setting aside that ex-parte decree the defendant No. 1 filed that Miscellaneous Case No. 47 of 2004. However, in view of the above quoted statements of the defendant No. 1 which he made in that Miscellaneous Case No. 47 of 2004 there remains no roam for argument that the defendant No. 1 did not admit the signature appearing in the impugned bainapatra as his own.
